title: LLMs & AI Agents
subtitle: Build, secure, evaluate and deploy applications on large language models
audience_line: Developers who want to build applications with large language models
overview: This programme teaches developers to build applications on large language models and to put them into production responsibly. Participants learn how Transformers and LLMs are trained and where their limits are, write effective prompts and structured outputs, use hosted APIs and open models, build retrieval-augmented generation over their own documents, and give models tools through function calling, agent frameworks and the Model Context Protocol. They then defend the application against prompt injection, evaluate it with test sets and LLM judges, trace its cost and serve it as an API. The programme closes with a final project: an agent application built, evaluated and presented by each team.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Developers who want to build applications with large language models

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Python programming (course: Python Programming Fundamentals, or equivalent). No machine learning background needed

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 27 h: 24 h of chapters + 3 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs; one application carried through every phase

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant (16 GB RAM, Python 3, Docker, VS Code, Ollama for open models); API access to a hosted LLM provided by the organiser with a spending cap; no other account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can build a RAG and tool-using agent application, protect it against prompt injection, measure its quality and cost, and deploy it as a containerised API

phases.name: LLM Foundations
phases.focus: Transformers and training, prompting, structured output, APIs and open models
phases.intro: Participants learn how LLMs are built, from attention and tokens to pretraining, instruction tuning and preference optimisation, and what reasoning models change. They then write prompts that work, get structured output, and call both hosted APIs and open models running locally. Validated lab: the same extraction task solved with a hosted model and a local open model, returning validated JSON.

chapters.title: Transformers & LLMs
chapters.content: Attention, tokens, pretraining, instruction tuning, RLHF and DPO, reasoning models, model landscape

chapters.title: Using Models
chapters.content: LLM APIs, structured outputs, open models (Ollama, Hugging Face)

phases.name: RAG & Agents
phases.focus: Embeddings, vector stores, retrieval and reranking, tool use, agent frameworks
phases.intro: Participants ground answers in their own documents with retrieval-augmented generation, from embeddings and chunking to hybrid retrieval, reranking and RAG evaluation, then let models act through tool use and function calling, planning, and multi-agent frameworks such as LangGraph and CrewAI. Validated lab: a question-answering assistant over a document set that cites its sources, extended into an agent that calls two tools.

chapters.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
chapters.content: Embeddings, vector stores, chunking, hybrid retrieval, reranking, RAG evaluation

chapters.title: Agents
chapters.content: Tool use, function calling, planning, multi-agent frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI)

phases.name: MCP, Security & Evaluation
phases.focus: Model Context Protocol, prompt injection and guardrails, evaluation, tracing, deployment
phases.intro: Participants expose tools through the Model Context Protocol, defend the application against prompt injection and the other OWASP risks for LLM applications, then measure quality with evaluation sets and LLM-as-judge, trace calls and cost, and serve the application as an API in a container. Validated lab: an MCP server used by the agent, an injection attempt blocked by a guardrail, and an evaluation report run before deployment.

chapters.title: MCP
chapters.content: Building and connecting MCP servers and tools

chapters.title: Guardrails & Security
chapters.content: Prompt injection, OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, guardrails

chapters.title: Evaluation & Deployment
chapters.content: Evaluation sets, LLM-as-judge, tracing, cost; serving as an API in a container

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: An agent application, evaluated and deployed
phases.intro: Teams of two or three build an agent application for a written brief, reusing the phase labs, then present its quality, security and cost as they would to a product owner.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, design the agent, build RAG over the provided documents, tools and an MCP server

chapters.title: Evaluate & Secure
chapters.content: Evaluation set and report, guardrails, tracing and cost per request, containerised API

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo including an attack attempt; questions and feedback

project.title: An Agent Application in Production
project.brief: An agent that answers from a document set with cited sources, acts through tools and an MCP server, resists prompt injection, is measured on an evaluation set with its cost per request, and runs as a containerised API.
project.stack: Python, an LLM API and an open model (Ollama), embeddings and a vector store, LangGraph, MCP, guardrails, an evaluation and tracing tool, FastAPI, Docker
project.deliverable: Repository with code and evaluation set, evaluation report, live demo
